YTA for a couple of reasons

| My girlfriend has said she often feels rushed in the morning and doesn't have time to put together lunch in the morning. I suggested she prepare something the night before so she can grab it on her way out the door

| I lack my own source of income.

Why don't you make her something? You seem very do as I say, not do as I do.

Secondly, get a job and your own source of income. Then when you have that you can talk together about putting together a budget. 

&#x200B;

Apologies if this comes off as harsh, but you seem to be over-dependent on your friend (I know you mentioned anxiety issues earlier). 

Your world should not crumble because your friend goes away for a week. Maybe look into some therapy to build your self-reliance?

I am from the UK so not everything below may be the same in Portugal.

I also dont want to tell you that you have a serious issue (it may be normal teenage hormones and it will pass) based on one post. 

That said, if you think some help will be useful - it will be useful. It is a sign of strength to reach out for help when you need it - not weakness.

I am guessing from your post you are school aged? If you have a good relationship with your parents I would suggest talking to them and letting them know that you are struggling a bit with some anxiety and have realised that you are developing a bit of an unhealthy dependence on a particular friend to deal with it.

If your parents agree the next step would be to talk to your normal doctor. Even if they dont agree, you can always talk to your doctor if you need to.

If you dont have a good relationship you could go straight to your doctor or tell a trusted adult like a teacher and talk to them.

You can also try some self-help things. I really recommend CBT as a tool that helps you conciously choose how you respond to situations rather than letting your subconcious make all the decisions.

Fundamentally you are responsible for your own emotional wellbeing. If you rely on others for that it will always end badly. You should want friends, but not need them if that makes sense.

YTA. I know this goes against most of the posts here, but seriously, if you do this you will be showing your daughter that you are untrustworthy, manipulative and not there for her.

You have told her you will pay and go! If you pull out of that for a butthurt reason like this you are definately TA

I know walking her down the aile means a lot to you, but do you really want to blackmail her into it? To know that the only reason she is doing that is because you held money over her head?

You can disagree about whether you think bio dad deserves a chance, but ultimately that is not your decision to make. 

It is of course your decision, but please know that if you do this, you may well lose your daughter forever.
Chidi?
Just to add - you are pretty lucky that the rent is being split 3 ways. It is much more usual to split rent based on rooms rather than people (utilities should still be split by people though).

Would your opinion be different if the OP was worded as this: WIBTA if I gave my stepdaughter an ultimatum to choose her bio dad or me? Because that is in effect what he is doing. 

Of course parents can be hurt, but this isn't disrespect or mistreatment. This is a person trying to connect with their biological dad. He may or may not be a bad dude. But you can't tell the daughter that. She can only realise it herself. Forceing her to choose is never going to be a good idea. If the daughter thinks he deserves another chance, then either a) she really believes he has changed, or b) there is more to the story than we know. 

If OP wants to show they are hurt and do this, that is there perogative. I was merely trying to point out that he risks ruining his relationship with his daughter forever over this and we may well be reading the TIFU by not going to my daughters wedding post in the near future.. 

&#x200B;

I put butthurt because OP's biggest concern seemed to be about not walking her down the aisle. 

He seemed fine when the bio dad was attending.

In effect he was saying I will only pay (changed in the edit) or attend if I get to walk you down the aisle. IMHO that is a butthurt sentiment.

NTA. My great uncle did something like this. He died without kids and basically "skipped" his closest remaining relatives to give to their children. His reasoning was that his cousins were all pretty much sorted with motgages paid off etc and the money he gave to the next generation could make a real difference to them. He was right.

Get a good attourney to draft the will though, as this may well be contested.

Personally I would do it a bit differently though. I would split the money by person (eg the grandkids get as much in trust as the parents do). You could give the parents the income from the trust to help with living expenses then the kids can have the trust when they turn 18? 21? 25? to pay for college a house etc.

&#x200B;

With $10m you could also some set aside for future grandchildren (to be shared equally when your last child turns 45 or something).

And OP is responding to that by showing her that his love is conditional. I think thats pretty shitty behaviour. I never said I thought she was doing the right thing by having her bio-dad take her down the aisle, I just think OPs response makes him TA.

>The time he spent forging something with that other girl could've been used to support his girlfriend.

> Maybe you're not looking for anything serious at 17, but still not okay to break up with someone and immediately move on. 
>

Basically i dont believe there is some magical minimum waiting period after a breakup. He would be an ass if he rubs her face in it and he is an ass for the timing
